Flag Football continues electric start to the season

Lila Carey, Staff Writer
September 19, 2026
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:39
Instaread

The Girls Flag Football won 39-0 at home against rival Niles North last Friday, Sept. 4, with strong performances on both sides of the ball. The Kits secured six touchdowns and shut out the Vikings offense, despite Evanston’s top defensive rusher, Camille Calixte,, senior, being sidelined with a thumb injury.  

The Kits’ quarterback, Ava Bellis sophomore, opened the scoring on the Kits’ first possession with a long ball past the Vikings’ defense to senior Brielle Rosemond for a touchdown. Bellis’ first extra point attempt fell incomplete, and the Kits would ultimately convert three of seven extra points in the game. 

“Today was one of those days where we needed to start well, continue well, and finish well, and we did that today,” Head Coach Carlton Rosemond commented.

For the Kits defense, multiple players proved able to step up in Calixte’s absence. Seniors Emma Reese, Mikayla Sewell and Nikki Dandelles, and Astou Cissokho junior, all brought strong pressure, often with two simultaneous rushers, and did not let the Vikings advance far. The strong defensive effort would continue throughout the game with the Kits ultimately recording seven sacks, the most they’ve earned since last Sept. 12 against Fremd

The Vikings’ quarterback, Molly O’Hara junior, a fast ball carrier, led the Vikings offense with several rushes. But the Kits defense did not falter, keeping up strong pressure and notching up several pass interceptions. During the Vikings’ second possession, Ella Martin junior knocked down two pass attempts in a row, leading the Kits to a quick turnaround back to offense. 

The Kits continued to receive on-point passes from Ava Bellis, leading them to five more touchdowns scored by Harper Wesenburg junior, seniors KyNia Hunt, Brielle Rosemond, and Katie Lidsay-Ryan, complemented by one rushing score from Bellis herself. 

Throughout this game, Bellis proved to be a key player. With zero interceptions and six touchdowns, Coach Rosemond described her as “surgical”. 

“If they don’t know about her, they should know about her,” Rosemond said, attesting to his quarterback’s skill. 

The game ended 39-0, a seasonal high score for the Kits. With this game, the Kits moved to a 2-0 record in the Central Suburban League and 4-0 overall. 

The next day, the Kits faced off against number eight-ranked Maine South and lost 24-12, bringing their record down to 4-1. Wins against Lincoln-Way East, New Trier, and Regina Dominican on the fifth, ninth, and tenth, respectively, brought their record up to 7-1. 

The Kits are currently ranked third in the state on MaxPreps, and are looking ahead to battles with second- and fifth-ranked Glenbrook South and Willowbrook, respectively, at the end of September.
